name: Turn-of-month long in index ETF
rule: Each month buy NIFTYBEES with full capital at the close of the n_in-th last trading day of the month; sell at the close of the n_out-th trading day of the next month. Flat (liquid ETF) otherwise. No stop. Test grid n_in 1..7, n_out 1..4, and anchor on monthly F&O expiry date instead of month end.
instruments: NIFTYBEES or other Nifty 50 / Nifty 500 ETF, delivery
holding_period: 2 to 8 trading days, once a month
reported_performance: US CRSP 1926-2005: 0.15%/day on days -1..+3 vs 0.01% other days (t=7.81), Sharpe 1.04 pre-cost. Nifty 2007/08-2021 (QuantifiedStrategies, 5th-last to 2nd day): CAGR 10.5%, max DD 26%, 30% exposure, price index, no costs. Nifty 2016-2025 (Zerodha, 5th-last to 3rd day): about 0.82% per trade pre-cost; flat in 2018-19 and 2024-25.
feasibility_reason: One index-ETF order each way; no margin, no shorting, about 0.10% round trip at Rs 1.5 lakh (brokerage Rs 20 per order, ETF sell STT 0.001%). Twelve trades a year cost about 1.2% against a gross edge of roughly 0.5-0.8% per trade.

name: Turn-of-month long in small/mid-cap index ETF
rule: Same as turn-of-month index rule but instrument is a Nifty Smallcap 250 or Midcap 150 ETF (test on the index first): buy at close of 5th last trading day, sell at close of 3rd trading day of next month. Skip if the ETF's 20-day median traded value is below min_traded_value_inr_assumed. No stop.
instruments: Small-cap or mid-cap index ETF, delivery
holding_period: about 7 trading days, once a month
reported_performance: Satish & Bheemanagouda 2023 (Nifty 50, Sensex, Nifty Smallcap 50, BSE SmallCap, Apr 2007-Feb 2023): TOM significant and 'more pronounced in smaller indices'; magnitudes not seen (abstract only).
feasibility_reason: Tradable with one order, but small-cap ETF spreads and closing premium/discount to NAV are unmeasured and can absorb much of a 0.5-1% edge; index backtest overstates ETF result.

name: Mid-month payday effect (16th day)
rule: Buy index ETF at the close of the last trading day on or before the 15th calendar day; sell at the close of the first trading day on or after the 16th. One day hold, once a month. No stop.
reported_performance: US S&P 500 1980-2010 (Ma & Pratt via Quantpedia): 16th beats all days except 1st and 2nd; 2.57%/yr, vol 4.31%, Sharpe 0.6; SPY 1993-2019: 2.08%/yr, max DD 8.62%. Weakening as US pay moves bi-weekly. No Indian evidence; Indian pay is monthly.
feasibility_reason: One index-ETF order each way; no margin, no shorting, about 0.10% round trip at Rs 1.5 lakh (brokerage Rs 20 per order, ETF sell STT 0.001%). Mechanism (semi-monthly US payroll) does not exist in India, so low prior.

name: Deploy new capital on monthly expiry day, not first trading day
rule: When adding or reinvesting capital into a long-term index ETF holding, place the buy at the close of the monthly F&O expiry day (from contract master: last Thursday before Sep 2025, last Tuesday after) instead of the first trading day of the next month. Compare with buying on the 25th or the 5th last trading day.
reported_performance: Gavhale 2025 preprint, Nifty 2003-2024: expiry-day SIP beat first-trading-day SIP by 0.77 pp/yr (1-yr windows), 0.27 (3-yr), 0.125 (5-yr), 0.03-0.07 (10-20 yr). PrimeInvestor 2008-2022 and WhiteOak 1996-2025 find SIP date makes negligible difference.
feasibility_reason: Costless change of buy date; expected gain only a few basis points a year at long horizons.

name: Day-of-week long in index
rule: Hold index ETF only from the close of the trading day before weekday W to the close of weekday W, every week. Test each W in Mon..Fri and a Friday-close to Monday-close weekend variant. No stop.
reported_performance: Nifty 1995-2015: Wednesday +0.16%/day in EGARCH (z=4.7), driven by weekly-settlement era. Nifty 2011-2018: no day-of-week effect. Mar 2020-Sep 2021: Tuesday and Friday positive. Nifty 2000-2011: effects vanish in 3-year sub-periods.
feasibility_reason: Mechanically trivial, but about 50 round trips a year at 0.10% is 5% a year of cost against an effect that changes weekday in every sample.

name: Sell option premium on Monday, cover mid-week (India VIX weekday pattern)
rule: At Monday close sell one-lot Nifty iron butterfly (short ATM call+put, long wings wing_pct away) in the nearest weekly expiry with at least min_dte trading days left. Exit at exit_day close or when loss equals stop_mult x credit. Skip weeks with Budget, RBI, FOMC or election result before exit.
reported_performance: Shaikh & Padhi 2015: India VIX rises significantly on Monday, falls Wednesday-Friday and on expiry day; March and December negative (period not shown; Thursday-expiry era). No backtest of the trade itself found.
feasibility_reason: One hedged lot should fit the account (margin not verified) but cannot be sized smaller; four legs each way cost roughly Rs 160 charges plus slippage; expiry is now Tuesday so the pattern may have shifted.

name: Overnight long: buy close, sell next open
rule: Every trading day buy the index instrument at entry_time (near close) and sell at exit_time next trading day (near open). Optional filter: only when close > 200-day SMA. No stop.
reported_performance: Capitalmind: virtually all Nifty points since 1995 came close-to-open; 2008-2020, 64% of nights up vs 46% of days up. Marketcalls, Nifty futures Jan 2011-Jun 2018: +595% gross on Rs 1 lakh; with 0.02% cost lost 67% in 185 trades (Rs 1 lakh) or made 9.3%/yr (Rs 2 lakh).
feasibility_reason: About 245 ETF round trips a year at 0.10% is about 25% a year of cost, above the gross edge; one Nifty futures lot (about Rs 16 lakh notional) cannot be margined and futures STT is 0.05% since Apr 2026.

name: Intraday short: sell open, cover close
rule: Every trading day short the index instrument at the open (09:16) and cover at 15:20. Skip if opening gap magnitude exceeds max_gap_pct. No overnight position.
instruments: Nifty futures or intraday ETF short
reported_performance: Only 46% of Nifty days closed above the open over about 3,000 days to 2020 (Capitalmind), but Marketcalls' author reports the short-open/cover-close test is 'not worth playing'; in up-trends longs gained intraday too.
feasibility_reason: Daily intraday round trips cost about 0.07% each, about 17% a year; futures lot too large for the account; mean intraday drift is too small.

name: Overnight short Nifty options (sell at close, cover at open)
rule: At entry_time sell one-lot ATM Nifty straddle in the nearest weekly expiry with at least min_dte days left and buy wings wing_pct away; buy back all legs at exit_time next trading day. Skip nights before Budget, RBI policy, FOMC and election results. Optional: skip weekends.
reported_performance: Bhat, Pandey & Rao, J. Futures Markets 2024, Nifty options 2017-2020: short-option overnight (close-to-open) mean returns positive and highly significant; intraday and open-to-open returns negative/insignificant; robust across calls, puts, moneyness, maturity, weekends; weaker on jump days. Magnitudes not seen (paywall). Delta-hedged, pre-cost.
feasibility_reason: One hedged lot only; eight option orders a night (about Rs 160-250 charges plus slippage) against a small nightly premium; gap risk is the risk being sold; option STT 0.15% since Apr 2026.

name: Momentum winners held only overnight
rule: Monthly: rank Nifty 100 stocks on 12-month return skipping the latest month; take top decile. Daily: buy the basket at the close, sell at next open. (Published version is long winners, short losers overnight.)
reported_performance: Lou, Polk & Skouras (US stocks): all momentum abnormal returns accrue overnight; other anomalies earn intraday; overnight-vs-intraday spread varies by about 2%/month with institutional activity. No Indian test found.
feasibility_reason: Daily delivery round trips in ten stocks cost about 0.6% per position per day at Rs 15,000 tickets (brokerage, 0.1% STT each side, DP charge); no overnight short leg possible.

name: Halloween / Sell in May
rule: Hold index ETF from the close of the last trading day of October to the close of the last trading day of April; hold liquid ETF from May to October. Two switches a year.
reported_performance: Global 1970-2003: 8.8% in Nov-Apr, about zero May-Oct. India: Sensex since 2000 averaged 9.35% May-Oct vs 6.92% Nov-Apr; Rs 10,000 from Nov 1995 to Sep 2015 became Rs 40,000 with the rule vs Rs 74,975 buy-and-hold. Nifty 2001-2025 monthly averages also favour May-Oct.
feasibility_reason: Two ETF switches a year; trivial to run, but Indian evidence is against it.

name: India month-of-year tilt: out Jan-Mar, in Apr-Dec
rule: Hold index ETF from the close of the last trading day of March to the close of the last trading day of December; hold liquid ETF in months_out. Variant: hold only months in strong_months. One or few switches a year.
reported_performance: Nifty 2001-2025 monthly averages: Jan -0.47%, Feb -0.74%, Mar slightly negative, Apr +1.94%, Jul +2.19%, Nov +2.50%, Dec +2.61%. December mean 3.19%, 73% positive over 26 years. Dec significant in Nifty 1995-2015 (t=2.45). No month effect in Nifty 50 for 2011-2018.
feasibility_reason: One round trip a year; but each exit is a short-term gain taxed at 20%, which can exceed the roughly 1.3% a year the averages suggest.

name: Fiscal-year-end dip and April rebound
rule: Buy at the close of the entry_n-th last trading day of March; sell at the close of the last trading day of April. Instrument: Nifty ETF (default), mid/small-cap ETF, or the n_losers worst year-to-date Nifty 500 stocks (tax-loss candidates), equal weight.
instruments: Index ETF or stock basket, delivery
holding_period: about 22 trading days, once a year
reported_performance: Trendlyne 2006-Feb 2024: April best month for most Nifty indices, up in 13 of 18 years (Nifty Auto 16 of 18); Jan-Mar quarter usually negative. Nifty April average +1.94% over 2001-2025. April not significant in Nifty 1995-2015 regression (t=0.6).
feasibility_reason: ETF version is one trade a year. The loser-basket version is marginal: about 0.6% round trip per Rs 15,000 position.

name: January barometer
rule: Hold index ETF in barometer_month. If that month's return is positive, stay long for the next 11 months; otherwise hold liquid ETF for 11 months. Test barometer_month = 1 (published) and 4 (Indian fiscal year, untested).
reported_performance: US 1857-2008 (Cooper, McConnell & Ovtchinnikov via Quantpedia): 10.38%/yr vs 9.98% index, vol 16.8% vs 19.2%, Sharpe 0.38. No Indian evidence; Nifty January averaged -0.47% in 2001-2025, so the rule would often sit out strong Apr-Dec periods.
feasibility_reason: At most two ETF switches a year; no Indian support.

name: Same-calendar-month seasonality in stocks
rule: At each month end, for every Nifty 100 stock compute the mean of its returns in the coming calendar month over the previous n_years years (lags 12, 24, ...). Buy the top_n stocks equal weight; hold one month; repeat. (Published version: long top decile, short bottom decile.)
reported_performance: Heston & Sadka, NYSE/AMEX large caps 1965-2002: long-short on 12-month-lag return 0.69%/month, 8.6%/yr, vol 12.2%, Sharpe 0.38 (t=4.19), pre-cost. No Indian test found.
feasibility_reason: Near-100% monthly turnover in ten Rs 15,000 positions costs about 0.6% a month, about 7% a year, comparable to the whole published premium; no short leg.

name: Pre-holiday and post-holiday long
rule: For each weekday NSE trading holiday H: pre leg buys index ETF at the close two trading days before H and sells at the close of the last trading day before H; post leg buys at that same close and sells at the close of the first trading day after H. Trade side = pre, post or both.
holding_period: 1 trading day, about 14-16 times a year
reported_performance: Dow Jones 1896-2002: pre-holiday days 0.239%/day; 6.39%/yr incl. cash interest. India: Lu & Patel 2016 (BSE indices, around 2008 crisis) find strong post-holiday effect and no pre-holiday effect. Nifty 2016-2021: only Diwali shows a significant before/after difference.
feasibility_reason: One index-ETF order each way; no margin, no shorting, about 0.10% round trip at Rs 1.5 lakh (brokerage Rs 20 per order, ETF sell STT 0.001%). Needs the NSE holiday calendar per year.

name: Diwali Muhurat session gap
rule: Buy index ETF at the close of the last regular session before the Diwali Muhurat session. Exit version A: sell in the Muhurat opening auction. Version B: sell at the Muhurat close. Variant: small-cap ETF instead of Nifty ETF. Once a year.
holding_period: under 1 trading day, once a year
reported_performance: Nifty 2006-2025, previous close to Muhurat close: up 15 of 20; mean +0.51%, median +0.30%, mean ex-2008 +0.21%. In 17 of 20 sessions the index closed below its Muhurat open, so the gain is in the gap. Small/micro-cap indices moved about twice the Nifty in 2015-2024.
feasibility_reason: One ETF round trip a year; expected profit after 0.10% cost is a few hundred rupees; thin ETF liquidity in the one-hour session.

name: Union Budget window: long day before and day after, flat on Budget day
rule: B = Budget day. Buy index ETF at close of B-2, sell at close of B-1. Flat on B. Buy at close of B, sell at close of B+post_days. Conditional variant: take the post leg only if Nifty fell more than pre_drop_pct over the 20 sessions before B.
holding_period: 1 to 5 trading days, once or twice a year
reported_performance: Nifty 2004-2023, 24 Budgets: up on day before 67%, Budget day 46%, day after 63% (Bank Nifty 71%, 50%, 67%). Average Budget-day move since 2010 +0.19% Nifty, +0.42% Bank Nifty; slightly negative in each of 2023-2025. One month after (2016-2025): about half up, half down.
feasibility_reason: One index-ETF order each way; no margin, no shorting, about 0.10% round trip at Rs 1.5 lakh (brokerage Rs 20 per order, ETF sell STT 0.001%). Two or three trades a year; 24-event sample cannot distinguish 67% from chance.

name: Scheduled-event implied-volatility crush (Budget, election result, RBI)
rule: At the close of the last session before a scheduled event sell one-lot Nifty iron butterfly (ATM short strikes, wings wing_pct away) in the nearest expiry after the event. Close at exit_day close or at loss of stop_mult x credit. Mirror test: buy ATM straddle long_days_before sessions earlier, sell day before event.
holding_period: 1 to 2 trading days, a few times a year
reported_performance: No measured study found. India VIX is reported to rise before Budgets and to collapse after election exit polls (headlines only). India VIX falls significantly on expiry days (Shaikh & Padhi 2015).
feasibility_reason: Defined-risk one-lot structure fits, but events are when realised moves can exceed implied; a handful of trades a year with all-or-nothing sizing.

name: RBI policy announcement drift
rule: For each scheduled RBI MPC announcement day A: test (a) buy index or bank ETF at close of A-pre_days, sell at close of A-1; (b) buy at close of A, sell at close of A+post_days. No stop.
holding_period: 1 to 5 trading days, six times a year
reported_performance: No robust drift found. Literature summaries: only unanticipated 'path' surprises move equities on announcement days; an unreviewed 2015-2025 dashboard of 26 decisions suggests about +0.14% in the 5 days before and -0.27% on the day (snippet only; values not rendered on the opened page).
feasibility_reason: Six short ETF trades a year; no evidence of an edge.

name: FOMC next-day long in Nifty
rule: For each scheduled FOMC statement date D (US date): buy index ETF at the NSE close on D (the Indian session that ends before the 14:00 ET statement); sell at the NSE close of the next Indian session. If D is an NSE holiday use the previous session. No stop. Eight trades a year.
reported_performance: Lakdawala (NSE-NYU), Nifty Jan 1991-Jun 2018: mean 0.33% on the day after FOMC vs 0.03% other days (constant 0.347, t=3.47, n=234). By period: 2000-2008 0.72% (t=4.65); 2009-2018 0.215% (t=1.66). Worst cases -4.26% (Sep 2011), -2.94% (Jun 2013).
feasibility_reason: One index-ETF order each way; no margin, no shorting, about 0.10% round trip at Rs 1.5 lakh (brokerage Rs 20 per order, ETF sell STT 0.001%). Eight trades cost about 0.8% a year against roughly 1.6-2.6% gross at post-2008 magnitudes; needs a maintained FOMC date list.

name: Lok Sabha election window
rule: Buy index ETF months_before months before the first polling day of a general election; sell months_after months after it. Conservative variant: buy at close of result day, hold months_after months. Hold no short-option or leveraged position over result day.
reported_performance: IndiaSpend: Nifty and Sensex were higher six months after than six months before each of the four elections 1999-2014 (average 40.8%). Ambit: Sensex about 33%/yr in the 3 years after three key elections vs 16% over 30 years; follow-through absent in 2015-16. Five or six observations.
feasibility_reason: Single ETF trade; next general election due 2029, so not actionable before late 2028; sample far too small to test.

name: Monsoon seasonal sector trade
rule: Hold a monsoon-sensitive sector index (FMCG, Auto) from first trading day of June to last trading day of September, Nifty ETF otherwise. Conditional variant: hold the sector only if cumulative Jun-Aug all-India rainfall is at least rain_threshold_pct of the long-period average.
reported_performance: Pandey et al. (Mendeley Data 2026), five sector indices: monsoon effects 'inconsistent and limited'; regressions insignificant; a Seasonal Long-Only strategy underperformed buy-and-hold. Regime-switching variants beat it in their own backtest (rules not published).
feasibility_reason: One sector-ETF switch a year where a liquid ETF exists; the evidence is against the simple seasonal version.

name: Expiry-week and day-after-expiry long
rule: E = monthly F&O expiry date from contract master. Leg 1: buy index ETF at the close pre_days sessions before E, sell at close of E. Leg 2 (day-after): buy at close of E, sell at next close. Test legs separately.
reported_performance: US S&P 100 1988-2010: 0.528% average in expiry weeks, 9.3%/yr incl. cash, Sharpe 0.61. India: Bank Nifty 2010-2020 shows no expiry effect on mean returns, volatility or reversal; other Indian studies find volume and last-half-hour volatility effects, mixed on returns. Nifty tends to be lower at expiry than on the next first trading day.
feasibility_reason: One index-ETF order each way; no margin, no shorting, about 0.10% round trip at Rs 1.5 lakh (brokerage Rs 20 per order, ETF sell STT 0.001%). Indian evidence gives no return edge before expiry; the day-after leg overlaps turn-of-month.

name: Expiry-day short premium (0DTE iron fly)
rule: On Nifty weekly expiry day at entry_time sell ATM call and put expiring today and buy wings wing_pct away, one lot. Per-leg stop when premium rises leg_stop_pct above entry. Exit all by exit_time. Daily-data proxy: sell at option open price, settle at final settlement, no stop.
instruments: Nifty weekly options expiring same day (lot 65)
reported_performance: No reproducible study found. India VIX falls on expiry days (Shaikh & Padhi 2015); volatility rises in the last half-hour of expiry day (Agarwalla & Pandey). Market changed: one weekly index per exchange since Nov 2024, Tuesday expiry since Sep 2025, option STT 0.15% since Apr 2026.
feasibility_reason: One hedged lot fits the margin (not verified) but is all-or-nothing risk about 50 days a year; needs intraday option data for stops; pre-2025 backtests describe a different market.

name: Quarter-end window dressing in recent winners
rule: entry_days trading days before each quarter end (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec) buy the top_n Nifty Midcap 150 stocks by lookback_days return, equal weight; sell at the close of the last trading day of the quarter. Reversal test: measure those names' return over the first two sessions of the new quarter.
reported_performance: IIM Calcutta thesis (abstract): Indian equity funds window-dress; risk-reducing dressing is about three times as common as buying winners; done mainly by poor performers. No Indian study of quarter-end price pressure found; funds disclose monthly.
feasibility_reason: Ten Rs 15,000 positions for five days cost about 0.6% each round trip; evidence for a price effect is absent.

name: Composite calendar windows with 200-day trend filter
rule: Each day be long index ETF if the day falls in any enabled window (turn-of-month 5th-last to 3rd day; FOMC next day; day before and after Budget; post-holiday day; Muhurat) AND ETF close on entry day > its 200-day SMA; otherwise hold liquid ETF. No leverage when windows overlap.
reported_performance: Quantpedia, SPY 1993-2019 (TOM + FOMC + option-expiry week + payday): 9.06%/yr, max DD 24.02% without filter; 7.47%/yr, max DD 10.14% with 200-day filter. No Indian test of the composite.
feasibility_reason: One index-ETF order each way; no margin, no shorting, about 0.10% round trip at Rs 1.5 lakh (brokerage Rs 20 per order, ETF sell STT 0.001%). About 12-25 round trips a year, 1.2-2.5% a year of cost.
